# Integrated development environment
The IDEs and editors commonly used for writing Go:

### 1. Visual Studio Code (VS Code)
- **Features**:
  - Open source and free
  - Supports a rich set of extensions, including the official Go extension ([Go extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=golang.go))
  - Supports syntax highlighting, code completion, debugging, formatting, linting, testing, and refactoring
  - Built-in terminal, making it convenient to run Go commands
  - Git integration out of the box
  - Rich theme and keybinding configuration

### 2. GoLand
- **Features**:
  - From JetBrains, a commercial IDE designed specifically for Go
  - Provides smart code completion, code navigation, real-time error detection, and fix suggestions
  - Built-in debugger, supporting breakpoint debugging and variable inspection
  - Complete refactoring tools
  - Integrated version control systems (Git, SVN, etc.)
  - Supports Docker and Kubernetes

### 3. LiteIDE
- **Features**:
  - An open source IDE designed specifically for Go
  - Lightweight with a fast startup
  - Provides basic code editing, debugging, and running functionality
  - Supports syntax highlighting, code completion, and project management
  - Cross-platform support (Windows, macOS, Linux)

### 4. IntelliJ IDEA
- **Features**:
  - A multi-language IDE from JetBrains; requires the Go plugin ([Go plugin](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/plugin/9568-go))
  - Complete code completion, code analysis, and refactoring tools
  - Built-in debugger, supporting breakpoint debugging and variable inspection
  - Supports version control systems, Docker, Kubernetes, and more
  - Provides rich plugin and theme support

### 5. Sublime Text
- **Features**:
  - A lightweight text editor; requires the Go plugin (such as GoSublime)
  - Supports syntax highlighting, code completion, and basic debugging functionality
  - Fast startup and response time
  - Highly customizable, with support for many plugins and themes

### 6. Atom
- **Features**:
  - An open source text editor from GitHub; requires the Go plugin (such as go-plus)
  - Supports syntax highlighting, code completion, and basic debugging functionality
  - Rich plugin and theme support
  - Built-in Git integration

### 7. Vim / Neovim
- **Features**:
  - A text editor; requires the Go plugin (such as vim-go)
  - Highly customizable, with keyboard-driven operation
  - Supports syntax highlighting, code completion, and debugging functionality
  - Cross-platform support (Windows, macOS, Linux)

### Selection advice
- **Lightweight editing needs**: VS Code or LiteIDE both cover the common Go development features.
- **Professional developers**: GoLand or VS Code are recommended; GoLand is commercial software.
- **Vim enthusiasts**: configure the vim-go plugin and turn Vim into a comfortable Go development environment.

Which one to pick depends on your own needs and habits — try writing a few programs before deciding.
